s1.syndrome_frame: Postpartum headache with worsening course and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on noncontrast CT
key_facts: 31 days postpartum after elective cesarean delivery
Initial mild global headache developed 8 days postoperatively
Normal prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio

shortlist.label: Subdural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection over the left frontoparietal convexity

shortlist.label: Postpartum cerebral venous thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Worsening headache and presence of a hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on CT scan

shortlist.label: Spinal headache
shortlist.why_kept: History of spinal anesthesia and development of headache

shortlist.label: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on CT scan and worsening headache

shortlist.label: Chronic subdural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection over the left frontoparietal convexity and history of worsening headache

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of worsening headache and the presence of a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on the noncontrast CT of the head are consistent with a chronic subdural hematoma, which can develop after a traumatic event such as a cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia.

rejected.label: Subdural hematoma
rejected.why: While possible, the term 'subdural hematoma' is more general and does not specify the chronic nature suggested by the timeline and CT findings.

rejected.label: Postpartum cerebral venous thrombosis
rejected.why: The CT findings do not specifically indicate venous thrombosis, and the clinical presentation does not strongly suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Spinal headache
rejected.why: The headache is described as nonpositional and unrelieved by rest or analgesics, which does not fit the typical presentation of a spinal headache post-dural puncture.

rejected.label: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: The CT findings and clinical presentation do not specifically indicate cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
